key_catalyst: US-Iran escalation entering ninth night with Brent above $90 and 30-year Treasury yield breaking 5%, intensifying the discount-rate pressure on QQQ's long-duration growth multiples
reasoning: The pre-market bounce on earnings anticipation mirrors the 7/14 pattern, when QQQ rallied +1.12% on CPI/bank optimism but then fell -0.27% and -1.64% over the next two sessions as geopolitical and yield headwinds reasserted. Today's macro backdrop is objectively worse: Brent has escalated from $86 to above $90, the 30-year Treasury has broken 5% (vs. 10-year at 4.60% on 7/16), and US-Iran strikes are now in their ninth consecutive night with a third service member killed. The market is explicitly 'looking through' these escalating risks in favor of earnings that don't arrive until Wednesday, creating vulnerability if geopolitical or yield pressures intensify before then.
